pages.text: Dorothy lived on the wide gray prairie of Kansas with Aunt Em, Uncle Henry and her little dog, Toto. Their house was tiny, and everything around it was gray. But Toto made Dorothy laugh every day.
One day the sky turned dark. "A cyclone is coming!" shouted Uncle Henry. Dorothy ran to catch Toto, but the wind was too fast. The whole house spun up, up, up into the sky!

Bump! The house landed. Dorothy opened the door and gasped. Everything was full of color! Giant flowers, fruit trees, a sparkling brook and little Munchkins dressed in blue. "Toto, we're not in Kansas anymore."

Glinda, the Good Witch, floated down on a soft white cloud. She gave Dorothy a pair of shining silver shoes. "To go home, follow the road of yellow bricks to the Emerald City. The great Wizard of Oz can help you."
On the road, Dorothy met a Scarecrow stuck on a pole. She helped him down. "I wish I had a brain," he said. "Come with us," said Dorothy. "Maybe the Wizard can give you one!"
In the forest they found a Tin Woodman, stiff and rusty. Dorothy oiled his squeaky arms. "Thank you!" he said. "I wish I had a heart." So the Tin Woodman came along too.
Then, ROAR! A big Lion jumped out. Toto barked, and the Lion began to cry. "I'm just a scaredy-cat. I wish I had courage." Dorothy patted his mane. "Come with us!"
Side by side, the friends walked down the road of yellow bricks: Dorothy, Scarecrow, Tin Woodman and Lion, and Toto too! At last they saw the Emerald City, shining green.
The Wizard was a giant head floating above a green throne. "First, make the Wicked Witch of the West go away!" his voice boomed. The friends shook with fear. But they would go together.
The Witch sent her Winged Monkeys, and they carried Dorothy and Toto to her yellow castle. But Scarecrow made a clever plan, Tin Woodman cried for his friend, and Lion bravely led the way.

The Witch tricked Dorothy and grabbed one silver shoe. "Give it back!" cried Dorothy, and she threw a bucket of water. Splash! "Oh no, I'm melting away!" cried the Witch, and she was gone. Everyone cheered!

Toto knocked over a screen, and there was the Wizard: just a little old man! "You don't need me," he smiled. "Scarecrow, you made a clever plan. Tin Woodman, you cried for a friend. Lion, you were brave. You had it inside you all along."
Glinda came back. "Dorothy, your silver shoes can take you home. Just click your heels three times." Dorothy hugged her friends goodbye. Click, click, click. "Take me home to Aunt Em!"

Whoosh! Dorothy rolled onto the soft Kansas grass. Aunt Em came running with open arms, and Uncle Henry waved by the new farmhouse. Dorothy hugged them tight. "Oz was wonderful," she said, "but there's no place like home."
